prism-screen.prompt: Concept art of the play screen of an original PC rhythm game, 16:9, seen as the player sees it. A note highway in perspective runs from a vanishing point near the top centre down to the bottom of the screen, divided into eight lanes: one wider turntable lane at the far left and seven key lanes. Rectangular notes slide down the lanes toward a bright horizontal judgment line near the bottom. Show: about ten short tap notes at different distances in two alternating colours plus one accent colour in the centre lane; one long hold note with a distinct head cap, a dimmer body and a differently shaped tail cap, currently being held so its body glows where it meets the line; one wide translucent band (a 'side note') lying flat under the left half of the highway, clearly beneath the key notes; one differently shaped turntable note in the far-left lane; a hit effect bursting on one lane exactly at the judgment line; a soft light beam rising from one pressed lane behind the notes. Below the judgment line sits the control deck of the 'gear' (the frame of the highway) and two side rails run along the highway's edges. The floor of the highway is dark and plain so the notes are the brightest things on screen. Background outside the highway: near-black. Style: cut optical glass and light. Notes are thick bevelled bars of clear crystal glass with a saturated inner colour (ice white, cobalt blue, amber accent) and a razor-bright leading edge on the side that touches the judgment line. The long note body is a hollow glass tube with a thin thread of light inside that brightens and flows when held; its head is a full glass bar, its tail a slimmer wedge-cut cap. The side note is a sheet of frosted glass with two luminous edge lines in violet. The turntable note is a faceted ruby-red hexagonal prism. The hit effect is a short burst of spectral light: a white flash, then thin rainbow-dispersion shards fanning sideways along the judgment line, gone in six frames. The gear is satin black anodised aluminium with chamfered edges; the side rails are clear glass light-guides carrying a thin line of white light; the control deck is a slab of smoked glass over machined metal with a small round lens in the middle. Judgment line: a thin white-hot line with a faint spectral fringe. Mood: precise, elegant, laboratory optics. Original design: it must not resemble any existing game. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no characters, no people.

r2-screen.prompt: This is a screenshot of our PC rhythm game. Redraw it as polished concept art in the same layout and camera, 16:9. KEEP exactly as they are: the lane layout, the falling glass bar notes, the blue judgment line and the position of every element. REDESIGN with far more character, all in one consistent crystal theme: (1) the control deck below the judgment line: now a rich sculpted crystal console, a large faceted gem set in a machined ring at the centre with light inside it, cut-crystal wings spreading to both sides with facet planes, inlaid hairline light-guides, small hexagonal gem studs, rainbow dispersion along the cut edges, engraved fine ornament; (2) the side rails: bevelled crystal rails with facets and a line of light, crystal end caps where they meet the deck; (3) the combo number and the word COMBO in the middle of the track: custom display lettering that looks cut from crystal, faceted bevelled glyphs with a bright edge and a thin spectral fringe; (4) the judgment text 'MAX 100%': the same crystal lettering family, sharper and smaller, with a small gem-cut underline; (5) the HUD around the track (song title plate top-left, SCORE / RATE / MAX COMBO / SPEED on the left, the gauge with its name and CLEAR mark on the right, the time): each set in a small chamfered glass plate with a hairline frame and a facet highlight, typography matching the crystal lettering, the gauge a column of cut crystal segments. Keep the texts the same words and numbers as in the screenshot, spelled correctly. Theme PRISM: cut crystal and light. Everything is made of faceted clear crystal, bevelled optical glass and satin black anodised aluminium, lit from inside by white light that splits into thin rainbow dispersion at cut edges; colours are ice white, cobalt and azure blue with small spectral accents. One consistent visual language across the gear, the lettering and the panels: 45-degree chamfered corners, facet lines, hairline light-guides, a hexagonal gem motif.  Original design: it must not resemble any existing game's interface. No logos, no watermark, no characters, no people.
